result.title: From Logs to Faults: Reference-Free Fault Localization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines
result.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines are widely used for domain-specific question answering, yet locating faults remains manual and time-consuming. Fault localization is challenging because RAG pipelines consist of interdependent stages, where faults can propagate downstream, masking their origin, or remain undetected even when the final answer is correct. Existing evaluation approaches often focus on individual stages and rely on reference answers or code instrumentation. We present RAGLog, which detects and localizes faults across RAG stages using execution logs, without requiring reference answers or code instrumentation. RAGLog transforms heterogeneous API logs into a common RAG schema and combines rule-based, embedding-based, and LLM-based checks to identify faulty stages. We introduce a live fault injector and RAGLog Faults, a dataset of 3,134 runs from five RAG pipelines with stage-level fault labels. With Claude Haiku 5.5, RAGLog achieves a pooled F1 score of 0.73 on runs with naturally occurring faults, outperforming Claude Code (0.58) and Codex (0.52), and comparable effectiveness on runs with injected faults (0.84 versus 0.80 and 0.82, respectively). It analyzes runs in approximately five seconds at US\$0.005 each, with overall lower cost and latency than agent baselines. RAGLog is available as an open-source tool for debugging, evaluating, and monitoring RAG pipelines.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 RAGLog，将 RAG 流水线的异构执行日志统一到公共 schema，并用规则、embedding 与 LLM 检查在无参考答案、无代码插桩条件下定位出错阶段，同时构建故障注入器与带阶段级故障标注的数据集。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无参考答案、按阶段定位故障并区分故障传播与掩盖」的诊断思路，可能可供核查于 LVR 中判定哪一步推理或哪一阶段视觉信息读取导致失败与贡献分配，但对象是 RAG 工程流水线，与 latent 视觉推理无直接关联，需较多核查。
